rationale: I own Lennar, and I see it as a cyclical, not the stalwart the screen suggests. Homebuilders are bought when earnings are depressed and the P/E looks high, not when the P/E is 10.8 and everybody feels fine. The headline PEG of 0.67 and PEGY of 0.58 look cheap, but they lean on a 16.2% five-year growth rate while three-year growth is -4.6%, so I don't trust them. Debt-to-equity of 0.27 and a 2.5% yield let me sit through the cycle at a small loss of 1.67%, and nothing here says my thesis is broken. I'm keeping the position at cyclical size and will not add until I can see inventory, margins and insider buying that point to a trough, because those are not in this snapshot.
